summary: The milestone completed 5 experiments in 5.2 minutes. The synthesis-only V608 post-marker source delta and compatibility audit occupied 5.0 minutes, while the sole compute-bound entry, V608 executable contract and bounded-shard preflight, occupied 0.24 minutes; no phase-level data explain either runtime, and the locked compute-task idle indicator is false.
bottlenecks_identified: V608 post-marker source delta and compatibility audit formed the critical path at 5.0 minutes; the available timing does not identify which internal phase consumed that time.
Disk-modification-time reconstruction provides completion ordering but no task-owned phase durations, limiting causal diagnosis.
No task-scoped model-concurrency or runner-selection receipt is available, so parallel-model DualGPURunner applicability cannot be assessed.
improvements_suggested: Add content-hash caching and incremental processing to the post-marker source delta and compatibility audit.
Emit task-owned start, end, and phase timing receipts for every experiment instead of relying only on disk modification times.
Capture task-window GPU utilization for compute-bound launches so a point-in-time monitor snapshot cannot be mistaken for whole-task behavior.
Record model concurrency and runner selection at launch, and select DualGPURunner only when more than one model is loaded in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Cache unchanged inputs and process only changed sources in the post-marker compatibility audit.
Add per-phase timing and task-window GPU telemetry to each experiment receipt.
Add a launch receipt that records model concurrency and the selected execution runner.
meta_reflection: The dominant elapsed-time entry is visible, but its cause is not: modification timestamps identify artifact timing without exposing internal work. Task-owned execution receipts would turn the next retrospective from critical-path identification into actionable diagnosis.
